title: The Archive Beneath the Storm

features.name: sediment-press
features.desc-on-touch: You feel the weight of a thousand storms compressed into text. Old dialect squeezes upward through the grid—words that the sky spoke before it had learned they were words.

features.name: rain-cipher
features.desc-on-touch: Rainfall patterns encode themselves as alphabet. Each downpour learns to mean something different. You recognize echoes of storms that fell before you were born.

features.name: compressed-speech
features.desc-on-touch: What rises here is not rain but the voices of the sky speaking its own dialect backward. Storm-speech that the archive learned to hear only after it had already passed.

features.name: storm-archive-door
features.desc-on-touch: A doorway into the sedimented record. You touch it and feel compressed weather—the sum of all the storms the sky has ever made, pressed into one thin plane.

features.name: dialect-sediment
features.desc-on-touch: Layers of old speech—each storm spoke differently, and the archive has learned to taste the year in every rainfall. You're reading weather as testimony.

inscription: sediment knows what the sky was trying to say; it remembers in layers, in dialect, in the weight of all the weather that ever fell

file.name: Storm_Sedimentation_Late20thCentury_Compressed.wav
file.note: Rainfall patterns from 1987-2009 encoded as audio compression artifacts; each corruption event marks a weather frontal boundary
